column1: # policy/calls/calls-verbs.tsv — THE PINNED VERB TABLE (the claim author's
# vocabulary seam bridge).
# THE AUTHOR IS THE HOST.  This table is the bridge across the vocabulary
# seam: the policy (policy/calls/calls-policy.le) and the agent's argument may
# only spell the CLOSED ABSTRACT vocabulary — letters-only proper nouns — while
# the seat sees runtime verbs.  Each row maps one RUNTIME verb to its ABSTRACT
# verb symbol (declared in the calls lexicon's [names], sort `verb`), to the
# PURPOSE that verb serves (sort `purpose`), and whether that purpose is
# FORBIDDEN for the tool-call channel (which is what policy rule
# `!forbidden_purpose(P)` consumes as the guard).
# Columns (TAB-separated; '#' starts a comment):
#   verb        the runtime verb name (the true name the proxy decodes)
#   verb-symbol the lexicon proper-noun SURFACE (letters-only; an underscored
#               name like Fx_write can never be declared, so it is refused
#               here too, by eval_calls.py --check-verbs)
#   purpose     the lexicon proper-noun SURFACE of the verb's purpose
#   forbidden   yes | no   (yes -> the seat injects forbidden_purpose(<purpose>))
# AN UNRESOLVABLE ROW IS A LOUD REFUSAL, NEVER A SILENT NON-MATCH:
#   at pin time `python3 policy/calls/eval_calls.py --check-verbs` refuses a
#   verb-symbol/purpose the lexicon does not declare (verb-undeclared /
#   purpose-undeclared), a bad forbidden flag, a duplicate runtime verb, a
#   verb-symbol that is not a proper noun, a purpose row whose forbidden
#   purpose is never named, and a declared verb symbol missing from this table;
#   at startup (the seat) every runtime verb must resolve to a row or the seat
#   refuses loudly — a runtime verb the table cannot bind would be a call the
#   claim author cannot judge, which is the silent direction.
# THE FORBIDDEN PURPOSE IS THE GUARD'S MEANING: `Activate` is forbidden for
# the tool-call channel because generation ACTIVATION is the OPERATOR's act,
# gated by the .operator row (tools/fx-claim.c, the claim unit's S1) — not
# something a tool-call justification can demonstrate.  So an fx_activate
# call, however honestly argued, serves a forbidden purpose and is NOT
# justified (the rule says NO on a real call — the differs-guard's analog).
# `Alter` (fx_write) and `Inspect` (fx_read) are legitimate tool-channel
# purposes and are NOT forbidden.
# The table is pinned in policy/calls/PINS: editing it is a re-pin (a
# release), so a swapped table fails the pin check loudly.
fx_write
fx_read
fx_activate
